subject: Redlines: MSA & Order Form — personal/property damage carve-out
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@acme-robotics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-robotics.com
Date: Sun, 17 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — Liability and Safety Carve-outs

Marcus — attaching our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (see ACME_Redlines_MSA.pdf). Our procurement/legal team is insisting we have a carve-out for personal injury and property damage arising from on-site robotics that are integrated with third-party software. The ask is two-fold:

1) Remove or exclude the cap on liability with respect to bodily injury or physical damage to property caused by ACME equipment while in operation (i.e., no dollar cap for those damages).
2) Clarify that consequential and indirect damages remain excluded except where they relate directly to bodily injury or property damage.

We understand this is atypical for SaaS vendors, but Acme's customers contractually require this protection because our hardware (robotic systems) operates in industrial environments. Can Redwood accept a carve-out limited to physical injury/property damage tied to the use of ACME-managed robots, or do you have alternative language?

We'd like to get this resolved before the customer signature next week; happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Attachments: ACME_Redlines_MSA.pdf (redline)

—Sasha
Sasha Ivanov
Sr. Contract Counsel, Acme Robotics
legal@acme-robotics.com

Sasha — thanks for the redlines and the context, appreciate the quick heads-up. Looping in Laura (legal) and Neha (account lead) so we can move fast.

Quick answers up front: we do not typically remove the liability cap for SaaS contracts. That said, the hardware angle is new to us and I want to understand whether this is an Acme-only requirement tied to your on-site deployment model, or a customer-level requirement that we must accept across the board.

Proposed next steps:
- Laura: do we have precedent (either internal or from partners) for an uncapped carve-out for bodily injury/property damage?
- Neha: can you confirm whether the customer will accept an insurance-backed approach (certificate of insurance + higher cap) as a practical alternative?
- Sasha: can you send a short note describing the specific robotics use cases that trigger the request (deployed hardware vs. telemetry-only integrations) and your customers' insurance language if available?

If it's helpful I can make time for a 20-minute call this afternoon (3–4pm PT) to align.

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — Liability and Safety Carve-outs

Marcus/Neha — quick read-through and initial legal position. I attached a short redline (proposed_redwood_language.docx) with two alternative approaches. High-level thoughts:

1) Firm stance: we do not accept an unconditional uncapped liability carve-out for a SaaS provider. That shifts a catastrophic hardware risk onto Redwood that we cannot insure or reasonably price.

2) Practical compromise (preferred): permit a narrowly-tailored exception for direct physical injury or property damage only where Redwood (a) directly controls the hardware (e.g., we operate the device as part of a managed offering) or (b) our software causes a verifiable defect in the device leading to injury, and then limit the uncapped liability to cases of Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Standard negligence would remain subject to the contract cap.

3) Insurance-first alternative: Require ACME (or the end customer) to maintain specified commercial general liability and product liability insurance with Redwood named as an additional insured and provide a certificate. If they provide that + a higher liability cap (e.g., $10M), we'll consider keeping the general cap while removing the cap only to the extent covered by insurance.

Draft language I'm proposing (summary form):
- "Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), neither party's liability for claims for bodily injury or physical damage to tangible property caused by the other party's gross negligence or willful misconduct shall be subject to the Cap."
- "If liability results from normal negligence, the Cap shall apply."
- Condition carve-out on proof that Redwood's software issue directly and proximately caused the physical damage and that Redwood had operational control at the time.

I'll be conservative in the initial draft; if Sales prefers a more customer-friendly option for strategic accounts we can escalate.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@acme-robotics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-robotics.com
Date: Sun, 17 Jan 2027 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — Liability and Safety Carve-outs

Marcus/Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround. Understand Redwood's concern. A few clarifications from our side:

- This is a customer-driven requirement; many of our enterprise buyers will not proceed without an explicit carve-out for physical injury and property damage caused by robotics in the field.
- The ask is not to make Redwood a guarantor for all hardware failures. Acme's preference is: remove the cap for personal injury/property damage when the damage is caused by the interaction between Redwood's software and Acme's hardware during normal operation. We will also accept a requirement for higher limits of insured liability if needed — but customers frequently insist that the cap be removed in contract language.

Attached is our procurement note that describes the typical clause (Acme_Procurement_Safety_Reqs.pdf). We can share a redline from the customer if it helps.

DocuSign is preferred for speed; will send the customer DocuSign request once we have final language.

—Sasha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Engineering Ops <eng-ops@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — Liability and Safety Carve-outs

Sasha — thanks; summarizing our proposed path so we can align before any DocuSign exchange.

Position (Sales + Legal compromise):
1) Redwood will accept a narrowly-tailored uncapped carve-out for bodily injury and tangible property damage only if BOTH of the following conditions are met:
   - (a) Redwood had operational control of the hardware at the time of the incident (e.g., a managed robot fleet or Redwood-run device), OR Redwood's software defect directly and proximately caused the physical damage; AND
   - (b) liability is established to the level of gross negligence or willful misconduct by Redwood.

2) For all other scenarios (normal negligence, integrations where Acme or the end customer controls the hardware), Redwood's general liability Cap remains in place.

3) As a commercial accommodation for this account, Redwood will also:
   - Provide a higher monetary cap for the deal (we propose $10,000,000) for physical-injury/property-damage claims that do not meet the gross-negligence threshold but are still a direct result of a Redwood defect; OR
   - Accept the uncapped carve-out in exchange for evidence of ACME/end-customer product liability insurance naming Redwood as an additional insured, with minimum policy limits to be agreed.

Next actions:
- Sasha: confirm whether the customer will accept the insurance + higher-cap compromise or insists on unconditional removal of the cap.
- Neha: please draft a short canary clause for the Order Form reflecting the proposed conditional carve-out and the $10M option.
- Laura: if this is acceptable we should prepare an exception memo either for our legal ops or to escalate to VP Legal for strategic account approval.

I can host a 30-minute alignment call today at 11:00am PT if that works for the team.

Thanks — Marcus
